title: QCIA Community Access: Going to the Shops
purpose: A community access AAC board that supports practical shopping communication, safety/help language, and teacher evidence notes for QCIA-style participation.

teacherNotes.modeling: Model real community phrases before the trip and during role play: greeting, asking where something is, paying, asking for help and saying stop/wait.
teacherNotes.evidence: QCIA evidence can note participation in a familiar community routine, functional communication attempts, help-seeking, choice-making and safety language.
teacherNotes.customisation: Replace shop/item vocabulary with the actual excursion, class enterprise or role-play context. Keep Help, Stop/wait and Finished stable.
teacherNotes.privacy: Use de-identified notes only. Do not record names, behaviour details or community incidents inside the generated files.
teacherNotes.safety: This supports communication during community access; it does not replace adult supervision, risk assessment or emergency processes.

systemFit.existingSystem: Confirm how this support sits alongside the student's established AAC system.
systemFit.vocabularyAndMotorPlan: Confirm familiar vocabulary and stable locations before classroom use.
systemFit.symbolFamiliarity: Confirm that each symbol or text representation is recognised and meaningful.
systemFit.accessCalibration: Confirm access settings on the actual device with the student and team.
systemFit.positioningAndVision: Confirm screen, mounting, seating, visual field, contrast and fatigue conditions.
systemFit.languageCultureVoice: Confirm preferred language, culturally meaningful vocabulary and voice output.
systemFit.partnerSignals: Confirm reliable yes/no, cancel, repair and partner-assisted signals.

symbolStrategy.customMediaPolicy: teacher-owned local media only unless explicitly approved
symbolStrategy.notes: Search terms are practical community/shop terms; local photos of familiar shops may be inserted by staff if owned/approved.

attribution.attribution: The pictographic symbols used are the property of the Government of Aragon and have been created by Sergio Palao for ARASAAC (https://arasaac.org), that distributes them under Creative Commons License BY-NC-SA.
attribution.note: Symbol search terms are provided for later ARASAAC replacement; confirm exact current licence wording when publishing beyond local classroom use.

sett.student: Student can use AAC to participate in shopping role-play or community access through greetings, requesting, asking, refusing, and help-seeking.
sett.environment: Classroom role-play, school enterprise, or supervised community context with adult safety support and local-first device use.
sett.task: Communicate during a familiar shopping routine while staying able to ask for help, wait, or finish.
sett.tools: Nine-button board, stable help/stop/finished options, spoken labels, text fallback, and teacher evidence notes.

differentiation.content: Preserve functional community participation while reducing speech and environmental access barriers.
differentiation.process: Model key vocabulary, provide wait time, allow rehearsal/repetition, and accept multimodal communication.
differentiation.product: Accept observed AAC selections, role-play evidence, photo/portfolio notes, or anonymous session summary.
differentiation.environment: Use a calm, predictable, local-first layout with teacher controls separate from student choices.
differentiation.support: Teaching, SLP, OT, family, and student/team review should personalise vocabulary and access before reliance.

participationBarriers.barrier: Community routines assume speech, fast responses, money handling, and environmental noise.
participationBarriers.support: Provide prepared functional phrases, help/safety language, wait time, and adult modelling.

evidencePlan.notJudgement: Adult safety support and access prompts are recorded as context, not as reduced QCIA achievement.
evidencePlan.export: Use anonymous teacher notes, print/portfolio evidence, or local CSV/report only when needed. Do not include diagnoses, behaviour details, family details, or school IDs.

provenance.sourcePrompt: Create a QCIA community access board for going to the shops.
